title: Colombia's Constitutional Court presents PretorIA (July 2020), an AI system that classifies and searches tutela rulings for selection; it was in user testing in April 2021 and still in use in 2024, with no published outcome measure
summary: Colombia's Constitutional Court presented PretorIA on 27 July 2020 to classify and search tutela rulings for selection, and the court still used it in 2024; no source measures an outcome.
account: In January 2020 the court's president, Gloria Ortiz, described the forthcoming tool to El Tiempo as Prometea, the Argentine system that inspired the initial proof of concept. Semana (3 July 2020) reported that the program was developed by the court with the Universidad de Buenos Aires and the Universidad del Rosario. In the same period the court unanimously decided to stop receiving paper files and to accept electronic filing from 30 July 2020. On 27 July 2020 Colombia's Corte Constitucional presented PretorIA at a virtual press conference organized by Corferias, according to Ámbito Jurídico. It is an artificial-intelligence system meant to support the selection of tutela (constitutional protection) rulings for review. The court receives about 620,242 tutela files a year (more than 2,500 rulings a day). PretorIA was to group, analyze and classify them by criteria that the court prioritizes. It was to offer search, categorization (initially for health rulings) and statistics. Developers claimed that it could process rulings in under two minutes, where a person needs at least a day to read 30 files. The algorithm registry of the Universidad de los Andes records a 2018 pilot and a 2020 deployment without quantified metrics. On 19 April 2021 Dejusticia published independent research with Derechos Digitales. The researchers found that PretorIA was still in a testing phase with court staff. It performed four functions (classification of lower-court rulings, search, non-narrative summaries and statistics), supported by a four-person in-house AI and data team. The court's 2022 management report shows that PretorIA stayed in use, with 42 trained categories, a new search engine and training sessions for the chambers. In a 2024 article, G. de J. Sierra Cadena, a member of the Universidad del Rosario team that built PretorIA, reported that the system reached 80 percent reliability in its implementation phase. In Sentencia T-323 of 2 August 2024 the court described PretorIA as a tool that classifies and searches the more than 3,400 tutelas that it receives each day. It stated that the tool neither selects nor prioritizes cases. No court statement of a verified outcome is among the sources. The court's PretorIA page shows no text.

data.retained_case_account: On 27 July 2020 Colombia's Corte Constitucional presented PretorIA at a virtual press conference organized by Corferias, according to Ámbito Jurídico. It is an artificial-intelligence system meant to support the selection of tutela (constitutional protection) rulings for review. The court receives about 620,242 tutela files a year (more than 2,500 rulings a day). PretorIA was to group, analyze and classify them by criteria the court prioritizes, offering search, categorization (initially for health rulings) and statistics. Developers claimed it could process rulings in under two minutes where a person needs at least a day to read 30 files. Semana (3 July 2020) reported that the program was developed by the court with the Universidad de Buenos Aires and the Universidad del Rosario. Alongside, the court unanimously decided to stop receiving paper files and to accept electronic filing from 30 July 2020. In January 2020 the court's president Gloria Ortiz had described the forthcoming tool to El Tiempo as Prometea, the Argentine system that inspired the initial proof of concept. Dejusticia's independent research (19 April 2021, with Derechos Digitales) found PretorIA still in a testing phase with court staff. It performed four functions (classification of lower-court rulings, search, non-narrative summaries and statistics), supported by a four-person in-house AI and data team. The Universidad de los Andes algorithm registry records a 2018 pilot and 2020 deployment without quantified metrics. No court statement of a verified outcome was reachable (the court's PretorIA page renders no text).

No court evaluation, metric or case outcome was found, and the court's PretorIA web page was not available.

fields.summary: Colombia's Constitutional Court presented PretorIA on 27 July 2020 to classify and search tutela rulings for selection, and the court still used it in 2024; no source measures an outcome.
fields.account: In January 2020 the court's president, Gloria Ortiz, described the forthcoming tool to El Tiempo as Prometea, the Argentine system that inspired the initial proof of concept. Semana (3 July 2020) reported that the program was developed by the court with the Universidad de Buenos Aires and the Universidad del Rosario. In the same period the court unanimously decided to stop receiving paper files and to accept electronic filing from 30 July 2020. On 27 July 2020 Colombia's Corte Constitucional presented PretorIA at a virtual press conference organized by Corferias, according to Ámbito Jurídico. It is an artificial-intelligence system meant to support the selection of tutela (constitutional protection) rulings for review. The court receives about 620,242 tutela files a year (more than 2,500 rulings a day). PretorIA was to group, analyze and classify them by criteria that the court prioritizes. It was to offer search, categorization (initially for health rulings) and statistics. Developers claimed that it could process rulings in under two minutes, where a person needs at least a day to read 30 files. The algorithm registry of the Universidad de los Andes records a 2018 pilot and a 2020 deployment without quantified metrics. On 19 April 2021 Dejusticia published independent research with Derechos Digitales. The researchers found that PretorIA was still in a testing phase with court staff. It performed four functions (classification of lower-court rulings, search, non-narrative summaries and statistics), supported by a four-person in-house AI and data team. The court's 2022 management report shows that PretorIA stayed in use, with 42 trained categories, a new search engine and training sessions for the chambers. In a 2024 article, G. de J. Sierra Cadena, a member of the Universidad del Rosario team that built PretorIA, reported that the system reached 80 percent reliability in its implementation phase. In Sentencia T-323 of 2 August 2024 the court described PretorIA as a tool that classifies and searches the more than 3,400 tutelas that it receives each day. It stated that the tool neither selects nor prioritizes cases. No court statement of a verified outcome is among the sources. The court's PretorIA page shows no text.
